questions.prompt: Labels look 10 days ahead and the test fold is days 20 to 39. Which training examples does purging remove?
options: Days 10 to 19 and 40 to 49, because their days overlap days 20 to 49
Days 20 to 39 only, because those are the test days
Days 10 to 19 only, because only earlier labels can reach the test fold
Days 40 to 49 only, because only later examples can leak
questions.explanation: The test examples touch prices up to day 39 + 10 = 49. An example on day t uses days t to t + 10, so the examples on days 10 to 19 and 40 to 49 overlap and are dropped from training.

questions.prompt: Why can a training example on day 38 help the model "predict" the test example on day 45 when labels look 10 days ahead?
options: Because day 38 comes before day 45, so it is the past
Because both labels contain the price moves of days 45 to 48, so the training answer holds part of the test answer
Because the model trains on the test fold as well
Because cross-validation averages the scores of all folds
questions.explanation: Day 38's label covers days 38 to 48 and day 45's covers days 45 to 55. They share days 45 to 48, so a jump in that stretch shows up in both answers.

questions.prompt: What problem does the embargo solve that purging alone does not?
options: It removes the test examples whose labels run past the end of the data
It makes every fold the same size
It stops training examples after the test fold from using test-period prices in features that look back
It removes training examples before the test fold whose labels overlap it
questions.explanation: A feature such as the past 5-day return on day 72 uses days 67 to 72, inside the test labels. Dropping days 70 to 74 after the test fold removes that leak.
